display.purpose: The chord heard or practised, tuner note, countdown, score. One per view.

headline.purpose: Page titles, sheet chord name, mic-gate titles.

label.purpose: Chips, switches, toggles, nav, field labels.

stamp.purpose: Voicing class labels only (OPEN, CLOSED, BARRE · 1FR).

fret-notation.purpose: Printed fret band on library cards.

shadows.name: envelope
shadows.purpose: Resting state of every card, panel and mic gate.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Hovered library card and the tuner string being heard.

motion.name: string-ring
motion.value: 1.1s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), translateX damped 1.6px to 0, staggered per string by note onset
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: sounded strings shimmer in strum order. Off under reduced motion.

motion.name: stamp-in
motion.value: 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), scale 1.12 to 1, rotate -3deg, fade in
motion.purpose: Clean stamp and countdown numbers landing. Off under reduced motion.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Card lift and control state changes.

narrative.overview:
Chordhub is printed like the packaging a set of guitar strings comes in: black ink on cool, slightly green-grey envelope stock, each chord sealed in its own white envelope with a perforated tear line between the label and the contents. The interface is ink and paper. The only colour in the whole system is on the strings themselves, in the six ball-end colours a colour-coded string set uses, drawn at the real weights of a 12-53 acoustic set so the low E reads heavy and the high E hairline.

Density is generous and glanceable, because the player has a guitar in their lap and at most one hand free. Chord names and gauge-style numerals are set huge in Barlow Condensed, the way a string pack prints its gauges; everything else is quiet Barlow at reading size. Motion is nearly absent: one authored movement, the strings shimmering in strum order when a chord sounds, plus an ink stamp landing when a chord is played clean.

The system is light-only by decision. It refuses the dark neon fretboard that guitar apps default to, and it refuses the stock white card grid: cards here are envelopes, with tear lines, stamps and printed fret notation, not generic tiles.
keyCharacteristics: Ink on envelope stock; white envelope cards with a perforated tear line and half-circle notches.
Colour lives only on strings, in fixed ball-end order, at real gauge weights.
Barlow Condensed for every name and numeral; Barlow for prose and controls; tabular figures everywhere.
Outlined ink stamps for classification labels; a rotated green stamp for success.
Selected state is always solid ink with stock-coloured text.
One authored motion (string shimmer), honouring reduced motion.

rules.name: The Strings-Only Rule
rules.body: The six string colours appear only on a string or a direct readout of one string. Never on buttons, headings, chips, backgrounds, charts or decoration. The palette rarity is the identity.

rules.name: The Fixed Order Rule
rules.body: String colour is bound to string index (low E red through high E violet) and never reassigned, reordered or used out of sequence. Left-handed mode mirrors the position, not the colour.

rules.name: The Paired Signal Rule
rules.body: Hit green and miss red never carry meaning alone: every use pairs with an icon (check, cross, arrow) or a word ("Clean", "In tune", "missed").

rules.name: The Chord Name Rule
rules.body: A chord name is set root at full size and quality one step down (0.62em, minimum 0.8rem, weight 600), tight tracking, as chord charts set it. Always use the same component; never type a chord name as plain text in a heading.

rules.name: The Condensed-for-Numerals Rule
rules.body: Note names, gauges, fret numbers, bpm, cents, scores and finger numbers are Barlow Condensed. Sentences are never Barlow Condensed.

rules.name: The Resting Envelope Rule
rules.body: Surfaces carry the envelope shadow at rest and gain lift only as a response to state. There is no third elevation.

dos: Do draw every string in its ball-end colour at its gauge weight (3.7 / 2.95 / 2.25 / 1.7 / 1.12 / 0.85, low E to high E), anywhere a string appears.
Do set every chord name, note name and numeral in Barlow Condensed via the chord-name pattern (root full size, quality at 0.62em).
Do put new content in a white envelope panel with a rule border and the envelope shadow, and separate a card's label from its contents with the perforated tear line.
Do show selection as solid ink with stock-coloured text, for chips, toggles, list items and the current progression step alike.
Do pair hit green and miss red with an icon or word every time.
Do keep the string shimmer and stamp-in as the only authored animations, and disable both under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do size primary actions at 48px tall when they are used mid-play.
donts: Don't use any string colour on a button, heading, chip, badge, background, chart bar or illustration; the Listen chromagram is ink and ink-soft for that reason.
Don't add a dark theme or a dark neon fretboard; the system is light-only by decision.
Don't fall back to a stock white card grid: a card without a tear line, stamp or printed notation is not an envelope.
Don't add a third shadow or a hard offset shadow; envelope at rest, lift on response, nothing else.
Don't use stamps as eyebrows or section kickers above headings; a stamp classifies a specific chord voicing or marks a result.
Don't introduce a second accent colour for emphasis; emphasis is an ink fill.
